# beowulf-fitt-34 — review, Pass 1

Reviewer: adversarial pass 1. Checked in the order set: grammar labels in notes, OE to `l`, `l` to `i`, remembered English in `i`, consistency with published parts. Only `units.json` fields `l`, `i`, `n` were edited, by script; `t`, `ln`, `v`, `p` verified unchanged. 21 of 32 units changed.

## Changes made (line · field · severity · what was wrong · what done)

1. 2391 · n · high · Said ‘gemunde’ takes the genitive ‘ðæs lēodhryres’. The object of ‘gemunde’ is ‘lēan’; ‘ðæs lēodhryres’ is a genitive depending on ‘lēan’. · Rewrote: ‘lēan’ is the object, ‘ðæs lēodhryres’ depends on it.
2. 2393 · n · medium · Apparatus form given as ‘sǣsīde’; Klaeber's apparatus has ‘sǣsīðe’ (‘sea-journey’), a different word from ‘sīde’ ‘wide’. · Corrected spelling and gave the meaning.
3. 2395 · n · medium · ‘hē’ taken silently as Beowulf. It may equally be Eadgils (nearest named man), and 2397 names Beowulf afresh. · Added the ambiguity and the reason it leans to Eadgils; l and i left neutral.
4. 2397 · l · high · ‘sceolde’ is preterite; l had ‘must fight’. · ‘had to fight’ (now matches i and note).
5. 2401 · n · high · Called ‘twelfa sum’ literally ‘a twelfth, one’. ‘twelfa’ is the genitive plural of ‘twelf’ (the ordinal would be ‘twelfta’). · Corrected to ‘of twelve’ + ‘one’.
6. 2403 · l, i, n · medium · ‘bealonīð’ was ‘baleful hostility’/‘deadly hostility’; fitt-25 (1758) set ‘bale-malice’ / ‘baleful malice’. · l ‘bale-malice’, i ‘baleful malice’, note adjusted throughout.
7. 2404 · i · low · ‘cwōm’ is a plain preterite; i had pluperfect ‘had come’, a force the OE does not mark. · ‘came’.
8. 2406 · i · low · ‘orleges ōr onstealde’ rendered ‘started the quarrel’; ‘orleg’ is strife/war (l has ‘strife’). · ‘set the strife going’.
9. 2409 · n · low · Note never said who ‘Hē’ is (a reader would take Beowulf). · Added: the informer.
10. 2412 · i · low · i ‘wire-work’ is a finer sense than l ‘wires’, and the note says it declines one. · ‘ornaments and wire’.
11. 2413 · i · low · ‘ever ready’: ‘ever’ is not in ‘gearo’. · Removed.
12. 2415 · n · low · Said ‘ȳð’ ‘wave’ was in the previous line; it is in ‘ȳðgewinne’, 2412. · Corrected.
13. 2418 · i · low · Opened ‘and there,’; ‘there’ is not in the OE. · Opens ‘while he bade farewell…’.
14. 2419 · l · high · ‘sceolde’ preterite rendered ‘must’. · ‘was to greet’ (matches i and note).
15. 2423 · n · medium · Claimed ‘Klaeber keeps the manuscript’; the apparatus does not give the manuscript reading. Also dropped the query marks on Sedgefield and Grein. · Now says Klaeber's text keeps ‘þon lange’ and keeps the queries.
16. 2425 · n · low · ‘scribe's spelling’ is unsupported by the packet. · Now says only that this is the spelling Klaeber prints.
17. 2430 · n · medium · Misreported the apparatus: Holthausen's first edition and Sedgefield put the name after ‘geaf mē’; Holthausen's later editions put it before ‘geaf’; and ‘Klaeber keeps the manuscript order’ is not in the apparatus. · Rewritten to match the apparatus.
18. 2435 · n · low · ‘frēowine’ called ‘the same word with a different vowel’; it is a different first element (‘frēo-’ noble, not ‘frēa-’ lord). · Corrected.
19. 2441 · l · medium · ‘sinned in with crimes’: stray ‘in’ makes gibberish. · ‘sinned with crimes’.
20. 2441 · i · low · ‘wearying to heart and mind’ turned a state (‘hygemēðe’, mind-weary) into an active participle. · ‘a weariness to heart and mind’.
21. 2441 · n · medium · Said ‘-mēðo’ would make the word agree with ‘gefeoht’, ‘a heart-wearying fight’; the apparatus gives no construction and the ending is not the adjective's. Scheinert is queried in the apparatus. · Stated only what the apparatus shows.
22. 2446 · i · medium · ‘when he must sing’: ‘wrece’ is a subjunctive in a ‘þonne’ clause, no obligation (and ‘may utter’ in l is not ‘must’). · ‘when he utters a lament’.
23. 2446 · n · medium · Garbled: ‘the noun gives gefremman its object, ǣnige’. The object is ‘helpe ǣnige’ (noun plus adjective). · Corrected.
24. 2455 · n · high · ‘berofene’ called a participle of ‘berēafian’; it is the strong participle of ‘berēofan’, agreeing with ‘reste’. · Corrected.
25. 2455 · n · medium · Misattributed the ‘rēte’ variants: ‘rōte’ with gloss ‘joy’ is Holder's (‘Hold.’), not Holthausen's first edition; Rieger shares ‘rēoce’ with Grein1; Bugge's ‘r(e)ōte’ is glossed ‘rest’. · Rewritten from the apparatus.

Count by severity: high 5 (items 1, 4, 5, 14, 24) · medium 10 (items 2, 3, 6, 15, 17, 19, 21, 22, 23, 25) · low 10 (items 7–13, 16, 18, 20) = 25 changes.

## Considered and refused

- 2428 · ‘frēawine folca’ as ‘lord-friend of peoples’ vs fitt-33 line 2354, which renders the same epithet ‘noble friend of peoples’. Kept ‘lord-friend’ (‘frēa’ lord; Klaeber's and Bosworth–Toller's gloss ‘lord and friend’). Not edited in a published part; flag to the owner: fitt-33 diverges from the lexica and the formula should be settled, then added to the house table.
- 2415 ‘no easy bargain’ (i): checked as a remembered phrase. It is rebuilt from ‘ȳðe’ ‘easy’ + ‘cēap’ ‘bargain’, and the note shows the derivation. Kept.
- 2419 ‘restless and ready for death’ (i): ‘wǣfre’ is ‘wavering, restless’ and ‘wælfūs’ ‘death-ready’; each word is lexical. Kept.
- 2455 ‘bereft of joy’ (i) and ‘wind-swept’: built from ‘berofene’, ‘rēte’, ‘windge’. Kept.
- 2451 i ‘once death's hard need has had its way with the one’ makes death the agent whereas l has ‘the one’ as subject of ‘hafað … gefondad’. Refused: the note already says the sentence is the hardest of the passage and glosses it as ‘he has undergone what death does’, which the i carries; any tighter rendering would invent a sense for ‘dǣda gefondad’.
- 2451 i ‘another heir’ (singular) vs l ‘heirs’. Refused: ‘ōðres’ is singular, and ‘yrfeweardas’ is the thing awaited; i reads naturally and does not change the sense.
- 2415 l ‘to be got by any of men’ vs note ‘for any of men’. Refused: the dative ‘ǣnịgum’ with the inflected infinitive is interest or agent; both are defensible.
- 2435 i ‘struck … missed his mark, and killed’ reads as three events. Refused: it follows the three verbs ‘geswencte, miste, ofscēt’ in order; the note explains ‘mercels’ is a guess.
- 2418 note ‘offered health’ vs l ‘proclaimed health’. Not a contradiction: ‘ābēodan’ is glossed ‘announce, offer’ in the note itself.
- 2444 i ‘swing on the gallows’ for ‘rīde’: the note states the OE image (‘ride’); the idiomatic line may choose the English verb. Kept.
- 2409 ‘ānne’ (‘a certain’ vs ‘sole’): note already records both.
- 2406 note sentence ‘What ‘ðonon’ looks back to is not shown.’ Vague but true; left.
- 2395 ‘binēat’ ‘benīotan’: lemma spelling is a variant of ‘benēotan’; harmless, left.
- Number-of-units/ceiling: all units are at or under eight lines; the 2435 unit (six lines) is within the ceiling.
- House table and published parts: ‘maþelade’ (2425), ‘gūðrǣs’ war-rush/onslaught, ‘hēan’ abject, ‘wyrm’ worm/dragon, ‘gold-friend’, ‘hæleð’ heroes, ‘fǣhð’ feud, ‘hordweard/linnan’ were all checked against the published parts and agree.

Verified against the source: line 2243 (‘nīwe be næsse’), 2262 (‘Næs hearpan wyn, gomen glēobēames’), 2388 (‘Heardrēd læg’), 2387 (‘Ongẹnðīoes bearn’), 2380 (sons of Ohthere), and the section numeral XXXIIII at 2391 are all as the notes say.


# beowulf-fitt-34 — review, Pass 2

Reviewer: adversarial pass 2. Re-read every unit against Klaeber's line and the apparatus (grammar claims in the notes, then Old English to `l` word by word, `l` to `i`, remembered English in `i`, house renderings), re-checked that the pass-1 edits introduced no new error (none found; the pass-1 corrections to 2391, 2397, 2401, 2403, 2455 were re-verified against the lines), then checked every entry of `gloss.json` against the line where the form stands. Only `l`, `i`, `n` of `units.json` and entries of `gloss.json` were edited, by script; `t`, `ln`, `v`, `p` verified byte-identical to the pre-pass file. `__broaden__`: all 30 values (29 as received, plus `wyrme` added) begin with the old entry whole from `known-forms.json`, then ` · `. All 104 novel forms are present; no entry carries a line number or ‘here’ (the only ‘here’ is inside the old `fæder` entry, untouched).

### Decision: ‘frēawine’ and fitt-33 (2354)

Klaeber prints ‘frēawine’ at 2354 (fitt-33), 2429 and 2438 (here). ‘frēa-’ is ‘lord’; ‘frēo-’ (‘free, noble’) is the variant Bugge and Trautmann print at 2438, and the one fitt-06 (429) renders ‘noble friend’ for printed ‘frēowine’. Fitt-33's ‘noble friend of peoples’ for printed ‘frēawine’ therefore renders a word Klaeber does not print there. Decision: this part keeps `l` ‘lord-friend’, `i` ‘lord and friend’ (2428; at 2438 `i` ‘lord and brother’ because the lord is Hæðcyn's brother), and the note at 2435 keeps the ‘frēowine’ = ‘noble friend’ distinction. Fitt-33 is published and not edited here; its 2354 unit should be changed to ‘lord-friend of peoples’ (and the glossary's old `frēawine` entry, ‘lord and friend, noble friend’, which cannot be rewritten, is now broadened with the accusative reading). Both forms go in the house table (below).

### Considered and refused

- 2435 · `i` makes ‘struck … missed his mark, and killed’ three events. Refused again (pass 1 reasoning): it follows ‘geswencte, miste, ofscēt’ in order.
- 2451 · `i` makes death the agent where `l` has ‘the one’ as subject. Refused again: ‘se ān … dǣda gefondad’ is the crux; the `i` carries the note's stated sense.
- 2451 · `i` ‘another heir’ vs `l` ‘heirs’; 2415 ‘for any’ vs ‘got by any’. Refused again, pass-1 reasons stand.
- 2406 · `i` adds ‘them’ (‘show them the place’). Refused: the dative of the party is implied by the situation and `l` is literal.
- 2446 · `i` ‘while his son hangs there’ for ‘þonne’ (`l` ‘when’). Refused: ‘þonne’ is ‘when/while’ and ‘there’ is only a pointing word.
- 2450 · `i` ‘away from this world’ for ‘ellor-’. Refused: `i` is allowed to unpack a euphemism; `l` ‘journey elsewhere’ and the note say so.
- 2403 · `i` ‘that threatened men’ for ‘biorna’. Refused: the note already declares it a loose rendering and gives the strict one.
- 2423 · ‘wæs … bewunden’ as ‘was not to be … would be wrapped’ in `i`: refused; the note explains the force.
- 2455 · ‘rēte’ treated as ‘joy’: refused any change; the note labels it a guess and gives the apparatus.
- 2425 · ‘bearn’ `l` ‘child’, `i` ‘son’: matches the house usage for ‘bearn Ecgðēowes’ in earlier parts.
- Remembered-English sweep of `i` (‘no easy bargain’, ‘full of years’, ‘heavy at heart’, ‘bereft of joy’, ‘hard need’): each rebuilt from a single Old English word or compound (‘ȳðe cēap’, ‘infrōd’, ‘geōmor sefa’, ‘berofene’, ‘nȳd’); no famous-translation echo found.
- Unit lengths, mid-line cuts and quotation marks: all within the eight-line ceiling, `t` cut from the packet, no straight quotes in `l`/`i`/`n`.

### Considered and refused

- ‘hygemēðe’ entry (‘nominative singular, jā-stem … some editors print hygemēðo’): now consistent with the corrected note; kept.
- ‘rēte’ entry offering adjective or noun: kept; consistent with the 2455 note.
- ‘hǣlo’ example ‘wished health’ vs `l` ‘proclaimed’: ‘ābēodan’ is announce/offer/wish; a gloss need not match `l`.
- ‘morna’ (‘contracted from morgna’) and ‘hoðman’ (‘dark place, covert; the grave’): unverifiable against a lexicon in hand but plausible and marked as guess where needed; kept.
- Old entries (sē, ðæs, fæder, sibbe and the rest) cannot be rewritten; their examples that come from other parts (e.g. ‘ðæs āhlǣcan’, ‘wunian scolde’) were verified to occur in the poem.
- Forms checked against the line and found right, no change: the other 88 novel entries, and the 29 broadenings (each new reading matches its line: ‘frēond’ 2393, ‘folce’ 2393, ‘sīde’ 2394, ‘syððan’ 2395, ‘ealdre’ 2396, ‘ealdres’ 2443, ‘linnan’ 2443, ‘oð’ 2399, ‘ānne’ 2399/2410, ‘dracan’ 2402, ‘bealonīð’ 2404, ‘wæs’ 2428, ‘ōr’ 2407, ‘nēh’ 2411, ‘frēawine’ 2438, ‘fæder’ 2429, ‘sibbe’ 2431, ‘lāðra’ 2432, ‘beorn’ 2433, ‘yldestan’ 2435, ‘wrece’ 2446, ‘ǣnige’ 2449, ‘symble’ 2450, ‘suna’ 2455, ‘wīnsele’ 2456, ‘reste’ 2456, ‘sāwle’ 2422, ‘sē’ 2406/2412, ‘ðæs’ 2410).
